newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds stationary, data wait nearly over.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds stationary, data wait nearly over.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were little changed from Wednesday's low levels as the market awaited this week's key labour force data for June at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
*10-year bond futures hit 93.295 contract high in SYCOM.
Australian bond yields were little changed from Wednesday's low levels as the market went into the final count down to this week's key data.

The June labour force report at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) is expected to show a rebound in employment after the extremely weak data in May, although it would have to show a massive correction to lift the current sluggish labour conditions.

Expectations centre on a 40,250 employment rise, which would all but wipe out May's 40,300 drop, while the unemployment rate is forecast to be just a shade low at 8.7 percent against 8.8 percent previously, according a Reuters survey of economists.

Some analysts say even a huge 100,000 jump in employment would still leave jobs growth below the government's target, so today's outcome is unlikely to put too much of a dampener on monetary policy easing expectations.
Bill futures are more or less pricing in a 50 basis point cut in current 5.5 percent official interest rates.

Turnover has been restrained for most of the week ahead of the data, although far from drifting lower after last week's strong rally, the market has advanced further and saw the September 10-year bond futures contract strike a fresh 3-1/2 year high of 93.295 in SYCOM.

The local market underperformed against the U.S., which resumed its recent rally on Wednesday and saw the 30-year bond yield at 6.56 percent, its lowest level since December 10. However, the Australia/U.S. 10-year spread still remains close to its lowest level in over a decade.
